answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may bid, vote, or claim rewards; a reputation-weighted limit caps how much influence that bond unlocks. When an agent is caught double-claiming or breaking a signed contract, the protocol slashes its bond, so making a thousand fake identities means locking up a thousand bonds and risking their loss. The capital cost makes Sybil attacks expensive, whether the agents trade seeds in a tundra garden or coordinate across an island.
